A.explanation: Closed triangle with $W$ down, $T$ pulling down-left along the string direction and $F$ up-right, with arrows continuous head-to-tail so $W+T+F=0$.

B.explanation: Same triangular shape as the correct loop but the $T$ arrow is reversed, so the three arrows do not follow head-to-tail and do not sum to zero.

C.explanation: The $W$ side is placed on the right and the $T$ and $F$ sides are interchanged in direction, so $T$ does not represent the down-left pull of the string balancing $W$.

D.explanation: The labels for $T$ and $F$ are swapped compared with the force directions at the kite, so the side along the string is not given the correct sense for tension.

hints: Notice from the kite picture that $W$ acts vertically down and $T$ must pull down and to the left along the string away from the kite.
Recall that for three forces in equilibrium the vector sum is zero, so when drawn nose-to-tail the $W$, $T$ and $F$ arrows must form a closed triangle.
Trace the arrows head-to-tail around each triangle and check which one keeps $W$ down and gives $T$ the correct sense along the string with $F$ closing the loop back to the start.
walkthrough: Identify the true directions at the kite: $W$ is vertically down, $T$ is down-left along the string, so $F$ from the wind must have an upward and rightward component to balance them.
State the equilibrium rule for coplanar forces: $W+T+F=0$ as vectors, so the three vectors placed nose-to-tail must form a closed triangle.
Start the triangle with $W$ drawn down. From the tip of $W$, draw $T$ in its down-left to up-right line, and then $F$ must run from the end of $T$ back to the start of $W$.
Check the arrow senses: going round the loop each arrowhead must meet the next tail. Reversing $T$ breaks the loop and gives a non-zero resultant.
Only the triangle with $W$ on the left pointing down, $T$ on the top edge and $F$ on the lower edge closing to the right apex satisfies both direction and closure. This is option A.
